order: Build the Quartermaster's deterministic P0 substrate: recorded allowance readings in, the router's bucket-state shape out. Give the module zero dependencies and keep it CommonJS, mirroring the existing verifier and router substrates. State must derive only from real recorded readings across both vendors — never fabricate a denominator — and leave ledger attribution out of scope entirely; it is impossible today and stays a registered follow-on. Keep allGreen() exported as a test affordance, and leave the router's wo7b score module alone. Leave modelAssist unused in this version; the substrate stays deterministic. Add no registry schema — the entry contract lives in this module's own README and nowhere else. Gitignore the two new runtime data files and keep them out of every commit. Prove interop end to end against the real router and wire the new suite into CI directly after the router suite.
claims: We shipped a 914-line module and a 637-line test suite: 152 checks, all against temp-directory fixtures — the real project data files are never touched. Interop was proven against the live router: a green state dispatches end to end, a below-reserve reading fires the reserve gate, an unconfirmed arm fires and a recorded confirmation lifts it, a hard throttle takes the exhaustion recast, and an exhausted bucket forces mandatory review to not close. CI now runs the suite directly after the router's, and the two runtime files stay out of version control.
